title: Crypto & Identity Acceptance Catalog for On‑Prem Air‑Gapped Rollouts
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Purpose: Define an explicit acceptance catalog for identity and cryptographic controls required to ship on‑premises, air‑gapped Redwood Private deployments. This PRD captures requirements, verification steps, and signoff owners for: SSO (SAML/IdP integration), RBAC and privileged role boundaries, audit logging and tamper‑evidence, and customer keying (KMS/HSM support + key import/export policies).

Background: Customers deploying in high‑regulation environments demand deterministic evidence of identity controls and key custody. Prior work (see PM-5120) covered access and crypto requirements at a high level; this ticket operationalizes those requirements into testable acceptance items and a lightweight signoff flow that can be executed by Solutions, Security, and Engineering during onboarding or GA readiness.

Out of scope: Full legal evidence packages for SOC2/ISO (these are handled by Compliance later). This catalog is an engineering acceptance artifact used to validate product behavior prior to customer onboarding or release to GA.
scope_changes: Initial scope included only SSO and RBAC; after stakeholder review we added explicit KMS/HSM integration scenarios (key import, HSM partitioning, rotation workflows) and audit retention/chain‑of‑custody requirements. We also narrowed the scope to on‑prem air‑gapped rollouts (not hosted) to keep tests reproducible in isolated environments.
acceptance_criteria:
1) SSO/SAML: Successful IdP metadata import and SP integration with at least two IdPs (Okta, ADFS) in a lab air‑gapped environment; assertion replay protection validated via time skew and nonce checks.
2) RBAC: Role matrix implemented with least privilege roles (Admin, Ops, Auditor, Service Account). Policy enforcement tests confirm Admin cannot bypass KMS HSM boundaries.
3) Audit Logging: Immutable, append‑only audit stream exported to customer‑managed storage; logs contain identity, request id, model/version, route, and token hash. Retention and WORM flags validated per customer policy.
4) KMS/HSM: Customer keys import flow works end‑to‑end; keys can be used for envelope encryption without exporting key material. HSM integration demonstrates attestation and offline key generation. Rotation tested with zero downtime for in‑flight inference.
5) Signoff evidence: For each acceptance item an artifacts bundle (test logs, commands, PRs, and runbook snippets) is uploaded to the onboarding folder and approved by Security and Solutions Engineering.
signoff_checklist:
- [ ] IdP integration test report (lab) attached
- [ ] RBAC role matrix document with bindings and tested deny/allow cases
- [ ] Audit export sample and hash chain verification attached
- [ ] KMS/HSM import and attestation logs attached
- [ ] Key rotation runbook and post‑rotation verification attached
- [ ] Automated test scripts (playbooks) for replay, rotation, and audit integrity checked into GH
- [ ] Security review completed (Security owner name and date)
- [ ] Solutions Engineering acceptance for customer onboarding (SE signoff)
- [ ] Release readiness checklist updated (release owner)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (lab): Execute full catalog in an isolated datacenter node maintained by Engineering. Phase 2 (pilot): run the catalog with 2 pilot customers during onboarding; capture timing and gaps. Phase 3 (GA readiness): incorporate fixes, finalize runbooks, and require signoff in onboarding gating. Rolling upgrades for customers must pass key rotation non‑regression tests.
test_plan: Test harness: provide a terraform/ansible playbook that creates an air‑gapped test cluster with one IdP simulator, a mock HSM (softHSM for baseline + YubiHSM for hardware path), and an audit sink. Automated tests: SAML assertion flows, replay attack simulation, RBAC deny/allow matrices, audit tamper simulation (corrupt a log and detect). Manual tests: HSM attestation using vendor toolchain and physical key import validation. Test artifacts must include console screenshots, syslogs, and command outputs.
risk_and_mitigation: Risks: HSM vendor differences can create non‑portable acceptance criteria; air‑gapped environments make remote debugging slow; adding HSM requirements may delay pilot. Mitigations: define a minimum compatibility matrix (softHSM + at least two hardware vendors), require detailed runbooks and an SE remote‑assistance playbook, and gate HSM mandatory production for customers who require it while allowing softKMS for smaller customers.
qa_test_steps: 1) Deploy airgap lab via playbook. 2) Import IdP metadata and run SAML login flow; capture SAML response. 3) Run assertion replay tool to ensure replays are rejected. 4) Create RBAC roles and execute access matrix tests. 5) Import key into HSM, sign a test envelope, verify attestation chain. 6) Trigger a rotation and verify no requests fail during rotation window. 7) Corrupt a log entry and run integrity verification script to ensure detection.
notes: Open questions: 1) Do we require FIPS 140‑2 level 3 for GA HSMs or is level 2 acceptable for pilot? (Security to decide). 2) Clarify whether audit export uses customer‑managed object storage only or both customer and Redwood mirrors. Decision log: added HSM attestation test after Engineering demo 2025‑11‑18. Next steps: Security to publish vendor compatibility matrix; SE to schedule two pilot onboarding windows (Jan/Feb).
